title: Adaptive session-affinity and windowed chunk pacing for SSE reconnects
creator: Ava Chen
description: Implement an SSE-centered reconnect strategy that combines per-client session-affinity tokens, a windowed chunk pacing (adaptive ACK window), and server-assisted gap-bridging so recovering clients can resume with predictable latency and minimal duplicates.
background: We currently support streaming responses over SSE and HTTP EventStream. Customers running long-running chat sessions or low-latency UIs experience two classes of problems on reconnect: (1) spike in duplicate tokens when the client retries without a clear resume boundary, and (2) head-of-line stalls when server-side batching obscures precise resume offsets. Existing tickets addressed resume tokens and chunk IDs, but operators still observe variable tail-latency and user-visible duplicate segments under high concurrency.
proposal: Introduce a lightweight session-affinity token (SAT) issued at stream start and maintained across reconnects, and an adaptive ACK window negotiated on connect. Key pieces:
proposal_points: SAT: server issues a short-lived signed token (base64) tied to stream metadata (client id, model, route). Clients include SAT on reconnect to get server-side affinity to same worker pool or logical session.
Windowed ACK: client communicates a desired ack-window size (number of chunks it can accept without explicit ack). Server uses this to pace batching and to build conservative replays on reconnect.
Gap-bridge hints: server returns a compact replay map covering recent N windows so reconnects can request a minimal set of missing chunk ranges instead of a full rewind.
Duplicate Tolerance: server stamps deterministic chunk checksums and sequence ranges so clients can deduplicate on resume if they already processed tail tokens.
Fallback: when SAT is missing or affinity cannot be honored, server falls back to existing resume-token based rewind with a short jittered backoff to avoid thundering replays.
Compatibility layer: endpoints remain SSE-compliant; we expose these as optional connect/rehydrate headers and a JSON handshake event at stream start so older clients keep working unchanged.
Telemetry: surface per-stream metrics: sat_issued, sat_handoff, reconnect_gap_bytes, avg_window_size, duplicate_chunks_detected for debugging and SLOs.
tradeoffs: The SAT adds a token issuance path and small crypto checks on reconnects which marginally increases control-plane CPU. Windowed ACK complicates server scheduling heuristics (we must respect small windows to keep latency tight) and increases state per-stream for a short retention window. The gap-bridge map reduces duplicate payloads at the cost of storing compact replay meta for recent windows; we cap retention to avoid memory pressure. Maintaining backward compatibility requires a handshake event which slightly increases client/server protocol churn but avoids breaking existing integrations.
acceptance_criteria: New handshake event documented and emitted at SSE start (schema stable)

SAT token issued on stream start and accepted on reconnect: when SAT present and affinity is available, reconnect resumes with < 200ms median additional latency compared to steady state under test load
Duplicate chunk rate on reconnects reduced by >= 80% in the replay test harness compared to baseline
Server memory for replay meta per worker bounded (configurable, default 4 windows) and verified with load test
Telemetry events emitted and Grafana dashboards added for the new metrics
Backward compatibility test: clients without SAT still receive full stream and can resume using existing resume-token flow

implementation_notes: We will encode SAT as a short JWT-like signed blob (no PII) with aud/model/route and a 60s TTL. On reconnect, if SAT matches a live session and worker has replay meta, server will compute minimal chunk ranges to resend. For security we avoid including session keys; tokens are opaque to clients. The ack-window hints should default to 2 for low-latency UIs and 8 for throughput-optimized routes; limit window <= 64 to prevent unbounded memory. Use existing KMS wrapper for signing to centralize key rotation. For testing, extend the streaming testbench to inject jitter and assert dedup metrics.
